# `docker_container`

`docker_container` asks Docker whether one container runs, through Docker's
own program, `docker`. The value of the module is the container's name,
such as `myapp-web`. A running container whose own health check fails
counts as failed.

MMWatchdog does not start a container. Restarting a container that ended is the job
of Docker's own restart policy, as restarting a program is the job of
systemd.

## Set up

The node needs Docker and its `docker` program. MMWatchdog runs `docker` as root, so
the check needs no membership in the group `docker`.

## Inputs

The module takes one value, which a check writes after the module's name, and no other input.

- the value of `docker_container` (string; required): The name of the Docker container that must run.

## When the check fails, and when it cannot check

A container that runs is healthy. The check fails when the container:

- **ended, or was only created:** `the Docker container myapp-web does not
  run: it ended with exit code 137`, or `the Docker container myapp-web does
  not run: Docker reports it as created`;
- **is paused:** `the Docker container myapp-web is paused: its programs are
  stopped where they were, and do no work`. Docker itself reports a paused
  container as running;
- **is restarted by Docker again and again:** `the Docker container
  myapp-web is restarting again and again; it last ended with exit code 1`.
  Such a container looks as if it runs at almost every moment, and Docker
  itself reports it as restarting;
- **runs, and the container's own health check fails:** `the Docker
  container myapp-web runs, and its own health check fails`. The body of
  the alert shows what the health check wrote last;
- **was removed:** `Docker has no container named myapp-web`. A container
  that is gone does not run.

A container without a health check, and one whose health check has no
result yet, are healthy while they run.

**MMWatchdog cannot check** when it cannot ask Docker, for example because the
Docker service is stopped, when the node has no `docker` program, and when
`docker` gives an answer that MMWatchdog does not understand. The run is then
unknown.

A failed run starts or continues the check's
[failing time](../../how-to/decide-when-a-check-alerts.md). An unknown run opens a
separate cannot-check incident after the check's waiting times, as the
design's [failing time](../../changing-mmwatchdog/design/checks.md#the-failing-time)
describes. The module reports no measurement, so the check takes no limit.

## Examples

```yaml
# /etc/mmwatchdog/check_groups/containers.yml
check_groups:
  containers:
    check_every: 30s
    time_limit_per_run: 10s
    alert_after_failing_for: 2m
    recovered_after_healthy_for: 1m
    checks:
      web_container_runs:
        docker_container: myapp-web
        alert_severity: sos
```

Every 30 seconds, MMWatchdog on the node runs `docker container inspect` for
the container `myapp-web`. While the container runs and the container's
health check, if present, does not fail, the run is healthy. The message is `the Docker
container myapp-web runs`, or `the Docker container myapp-web runs, and its
own health check passes` for a container with a health check.

When the container has ended, is paused, restarts again and again, fails
its health check, or is gone for 2 minutes, MMWatchdog sends an `sos` alert.
MMWatchdog does not start the container: Docker's restart policy does, if
the container has one.

## How it works

During each run, MMWatchdog executes
`docker container inspect --format '{{json .State}}'` as root. The command uses
the container's name. MMWatchdog reads whether the
container runs, is paused, or restarts, and the container's exit code.
For a container with a health check, MMWatchdog also reads the health
check's status and the output of the health check's last run.

A container whose health check has no result yet is healthy. The message is
`the Docker container myapp-web runs, and its own health check has no result yet`.

## Errors and what they mean

- **`check_groups.containers.checks.web_container_runs.docker_container: must
  be the name of a Docker container, such as myapp-web`.** A container's
  name starts with a letter or a digit, then has letters, digits, `_`, `.`,
  and `-`, and has at most 255 characters.
- **`check_groups.containers.checks.web_container_runs.fail_when_measurement_above:
  the module docker_container reports no measurement, so its check takes no
  limit`.**
- **`MMWatchdog cannot run docker: executable file not found in $PATH`.** The node
  has no Docker. The run is unknown.
- **`MMWatchdog cannot ask Docker about the container myapp-web: ...`.** Docker
  answered with an error, for example because its service is stopped. The
  message holds what `docker` said. Start Docker: `systemctl start docker`.
- **`docker gave an answer about the container myapp-web that MMWatchdog does not
  understand`.** The run is unknown. What `docker container inspect` wrote
  was not the state of a container in JSON.
- **`Docker has no container named myapp-web`.** The container was removed,
  or the name is wrong. `docker ps --all` lists the containers of the node.

## Tested on

[Limits on each distribution](../limits-on-each-distribution.md) says what MMWatchdog cannot do on each distribution, or did not test there, and why.

- **Go tests:** `TestDockerContainerCheck` in `server_checks_test.go` runs
  the check against a stand-in for `docker`: every state that Docker
  reports, a paused container, a failing health check with its last output,
  a removed container, a Docker that cannot be queried, and a node without
  `docker`.
- **Real Docker,** on [every target distribution](../../changing-mmwatchdog/testing.md#every-target-distribution) except Rocky Linux 9 and AlmaLinux 10, whose repositories have no Docker (it comes from Docker's own repository): the `services` suite
  (`service_scenarios.py`) installs Docker and runs containers of an image
  made from the guest's own `busybox` program, so the suite downloads nothing.
  The suite finds a container that runs, one that ended, one that is
  paused, one that was removed, and one whose own health check fails and
  then passes. A stopped Docker makes the check unknown. The latest run
  passed on those ([validation record](../../changing-mmwatchdog/validation.md)).

## Why it works this way

- **MMWatchdog does not start a container.** Restarting a container that ended is
  the job of Docker's own restart policy, as restarting a program is the job
  of systemd.
- **The check asks through the `docker` program,** as a core module asks a
  node tool through the tool's own program.
- **A paused container fails.** Docker reports a paused container as
  running, but the paused container's programs do no work.
- **A container that Docker restarts again and again fails.** The
  repeatedly restarted container looks as if the container runs at almost
  every moment.
- **A container whose own health check fails fails.** The container with a
  failed health check runs but does not work, according to Docker.
- **A removed container fails, and a run that cannot query Docker is
  unknown.** A removed container does not run. When Docker does not answer,
  MMWatchdog learns nothing about the container.
